## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet RT average settled at **$24.87/MWh** — a significant step-down from the prior two days ($74.66 on 10-31, $35.57 on 11-01), confirming the post-spike normalization that began on 11-01. The headline story is the **bifurcated price environment**: four nodes (MAINLAND_RN, GRDNE_ESR_RN, CISC_RN, RUSSEKST_RN) experienced RT spikes exceeding $100/MWh — with the fleet peak reaching **$986.43/MWh** — while simultaneously **18 of 32 nodes recorded negative RT prices**, the largest negative-price cohort in the recent 3-day window. This compression between negative-price West Texas / South Texas nodes and spiking constrained nodes reflects classic ERCOT transmission congestion morphology, not system-wide tightness. Assets that dispatched in RT at spike nodes (particularly MAINLAND_RN and CISC_RN) almost certainly captured outsized value; assets sitting at negative-price nodes during charging windows had a favorable charging cost basis if scheduled correctly. The 10-31 all-fleet spike event (32 nodes, $74.66 avg) now appears to have been a discrete stress event rather than a sustained regime shift.
